question: I forgot my password. How do I reset it?

highest_context_chunk.text:
Employee description: I can't remember my password and I need to get into the portal this morning.

Technician resolution: Confirmed the user had a registered authenticator app. Walked them through Forgot password at portal.northwind-logistics.example, MFA challenge completed, reset link used within the 20 minute window. Resolved.

answer:
To reset your Northwind password, follow these steps:

1. Open portal.northwind-logistics.example and click **“Forgot password.”**  
2. Enter your corporate email address.  
3. Complete the multi‑factor verification that is already registered to your account.  
4. The portal will send you a single‑use reset link.  
5. Click the link (it expires 20 minutes after it is issued) and set a new password that meets the complexity rule: at least 12 characters, with uppercase, lowercase, and a digit, and not one of your last five passwords.  

If you do not have a registered verification method (e.g., you no longer have the device that was registered), the portal cannot help you. In that case, call the IT Service Desk on extension 4400.  

[A01]

question: My account is locked, what should I do?

highest_context_chunk.text:
Most access problems are routine and the service desk handles them. Some cases go
to the Security team instead.

Escalate to Security if you believe your account has been compromised -- for
example if you receive password reset emails you did not request, or you see
sign-in activity you do not recognise.

A reset request arriving from outside the corporate network without multi-factor
verification is also treated as a security case rather than a routine reset.

Finally, an account that locks more than three times in 24 hours is referred to
Security, because repeated lockouts can indicate someone else attempting to guess
the password.

In these cases do not simply retry the self-service flow. Report it so that the
activity can be reviewed.

answer:
Your account is locked because it reached the five‑attempt limit.  
- It will unlock automatically in 30 minutes; you can simply try again after that [A02].  
- If you need access sooner, call the IT Service Desk at extension 4400. They will verify your identity, get manager confirmation, and can release the lock immediately [A02].  
- If this is the third lockout within 24 hours, the desk will refer the case to Security for review [A06].

question: I lost my phone that had my authenticator app. How do I recover access?

highest_context_chunk.text:
Employee description: I dropped my phone and it is completely dead. That is where my authenticator app was.

Technician resolution: MFA device unavailable. Verified employee ID and confirmed with the line manager, removed the old registration and issued a 24 hour enrolment code. User registered a new phone at the portal the same day.

answer:
Lost phone – Authenticator app no longer works

1. Call the IT Service Desk on extension 4400.  
2. Verify your employee ID and confirm with your manager.  
3. The desk will remove the old registration and issue you a temporary 24‑hour enrolment code.  
4. On portal.northwind‑logistics.example, use that code to register your new phone.  

Until a new method is registered you won’t be able to use self‑service password reset. [ A03 ] [ A10 ]

question: What are the password requirements?

highest_context_chunk.text:
Employee description: The portal will not accept my new password.

Technician resolution: The proposed password was 9 characters. Restated the complexity rule: minimum 12 characters with upper case, lower case and a digit, and no reuse of the last five. User chose a longer passphrase and it was accepted.

answer:
Password rules for Northwind accounts are:

- Minimum 12 characters long  
- Must contain at least one uppercase letter, one lowercase letter, and one digit  
- You cannot reuse any of your last five passwords  
- Passwords expire after 180 days (you’ll get an email warning 14 days before expiry and can reset via self‑service)  

[ A05 ] [ T09 ]

question: How does the service desk check who I am before resetting anything?

highest_context_chunk.text:
Before making any change that affects account credentials, the IT Service Desk
confirms who you are. This protects you against someone else requesting changes
to your account.

For multi-factor removal and for lockout overrides, the desk requires two things:
your employee ID number, and confirmation from your line manager.

Self-service password resets in the portal do not involve the service desk. In
that flow your registered verification method performs the same role that manual
identity checks perform at the desk.

The service desk will never ask you for your password, and will never ask you to
read a reset link aloud or forward it. Treat any such request as suspicious and
report it to the Security team.

answer: The Service Desk verifies your identity before making any credential change by asking for your employee ID number and, for multi‑factor or lockout overrides, a confirmation from your line manager. They will never ask for your password or a reset link. This process protects you against unauthorized requests. [A04]

question: My reset link keeps expiring before I can use it.

highest_context_chunk.text:
Employee description: Tried resetting my password three times and the link says it has expired.

Technician resolution: The user was opening an older email each time. Explained that each request invalidates the previous link and that links expire after 20 minutes. Requested a fresh link and the user completed the reset.

answer:
Open the portal at portal.northwind-logistics.example and start a brand‑new reset request.  
Each time you request a reset a new single‑use link is sent and the previous one is invalidated.  
The link only lasts 20 minutes, so be sure to click it quickly and don’t reuse an older email you’ve opened before [T02][A01].  

If you can’t use the link because it expires, request a fresh one immediately and follow the on‑screen multi‑factor verification.  

If you don’t have a registered verification method (or believe your account is compromised), call the IT Service Desk on extension 4400.
